text.p: Unidyne Corp said it bought Maxwell Dynamometer Systems Inc in an all stock transaction valued at roughly $5.87 million.
Privately held Maxwell, based in Exton, Pa., develops a technology used in vehicle-emissions testing. Unidyne had previously held a nine percent stake in the company, it said.
Unidyne did not disclose revenues or earnings for Maxwell. It did not say how much the acquisition would contribute to its own revenue or earnings.
According to Unidyne Chief Financial Officer Tim Flynn, Unidyne made the acquisition to increase its exposure in the emissions testing arena.
"Maxwell has the technology and we have the manufacturing expertise and capacity," he told Reuters. "We expect the synergies to make us a key player in the emissions testing area."
